content:
Hi all,

I've started working on an interface for sets.

My end goal for this interface is that we should be able to unify CoPset and gset from the Rocq version under the common interface to solve the problem of different algebras for them.
I'll post a more ironed version on Friday together with a draft PR, but sketch some rough ideas below:

  • The interface for general sets includes simple primitives: empty, insert, singleton, insert, union, intersection, membership with the usual axioms.
  • Finite sets are general sets of elements with decidable equality with a map to a version of Finsets from Mathlib that respects membership. The choice is motivated by the fact that otherwise it's not possible to instantiate it with ExtHashSet (see a related discussion). For similar reasons, I would argue that probably the same should be done with FinitePartialMap interface.
  • The requirement for decidable equality seems unavoidable, but also a bit more general than the one in Rocq, where being countable is also a requirement for elements of sets.
  • Algebra for sets is defined for general sets with decidable disjoint operation, which holds for CoPset and FiniteSets, which should allow to unify them.
  • Using Finsets has one drawback: fold operations becomes a bit more complicated, as the function argument should be commutative to respect Finset quotient relation. However, so far it has been used only in bigOps, where the functions are logical operations, which are commutative.

I'm happy to answer here or post code snippets, if there're any comments/questions.

Cool! Yeah this would be awesome. A note about decidable equality: It's no issue to require that a type has DecidableEq, because you can always Open Classical to get an instance (assuming you're not computing with it).

That's true! I am also wondering if it makes sense to bundle DecidableEq. So far, I've simply kept it in the context, but as it is needed not only for lemmas, but also for operations, probably it makes sense to add it to Finset definition.

Hi Sergei. Thanks a lot for the implementation of CoPset. I am currently working on fancy updates, and I have a question about the intended way to reason about equalities between CoPsets. For example, I am trying to prove:

theorem fupd_mask_frame {E E' E1 E2 : CoPset} {P : PROP} :
    E1 ⊆ E → (|={E1,E2}=> |={E2 ∪ (E \ E1),E'}=> P) ⊢ |={E,E'}=> P := by
  sorry

To apply fupd_mask_frame_r, I can prove the disjointness side-condition E1 ## E \ E1, but the main remaining step is to relate E1 ∪ (E \ E1) back to E under the assumption E1 ⊆ E.

Is there already an intended extensionality principle for CoPset, something like (∀ p, p ∈ X ↔ p ∈ Y) → X = Y, or would you prefer handling this later via the more general sets interface you mentioned?

Hi Yunsong!
The implementation of CoPset is by Remy Seassau, I'm just adding some things on top :)

There's an extensionality both for CoPset and for generic sets in the set interface PR.

Perhaps, it's better to build on top of the interface, so we don't duplicate lemmas for CoPset and sets.
Also, that would be a good test on whether the interface works well.

If you plan to build on top of the interface, there's already this lemma.
I'm hoping to merge the generic sets PR sometime soon, working on it today!

I’ll build on top of the interface rather than adding CoPset-specific lemmas, since that seems cleaner and also a good test for the abstraction.
